source.title: Weighted Grouped Query Attention in Transformers

record.tranche_reason: Compares downstream evaluation scores for T5-small and T5-base, bearing on whether downstream performance improves with model scale; it does not measure pretraining loss or fit a scaling law.
record.gate_note: The paper calls its T5-small/T5-base comparison validation of scaling laws, but reports downstream ROUGE scores rather than held-out cross-entropy loss. Only the matched CNN/Daily Mail scores across model sizes are recorded here. Other reported attention-configuration comparisons do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is an attention-variant (WGQA) paper, but it includes one incidental scale check. Fine-tuned T5-small and T5-base on CNN/Daily Mail give a two-point downstream comparison on whether performance rises with model size. Two sizes cannot show predictability, no curve is fitted and pretraining loss is not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say the T5-small/T5-base comparison 'validated our results with the scaling laws'. They conclude that larger models give better evaluation metrics, and state that the WGQA–GQA gap widened with parameter size and should widen further for bigger models.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes pretrained T5-small and T5-base with different attention configurations and compares downstream metrics; it does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit power laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The compared architecture size and attention configuration distinguish the reported CNN/Daily Mail scores.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors say the WGQA–GQA gap widened with model size: 0.0 R1 at T5-small (40.3 vs 40.3) and 0.2 at T5-base (41.9 vs 41.7). They extrapolate a larger gap for bigger models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of a fine-tuning-time architecture modification grows with model scale.

record.problems: Only two model sizes are compared, parameter counts are not stated, and the scaling evidence is downstream Rouge 1 on one dataset rather than held-out pretraining loss. The paper notes that it did not pre-train from scratch or fine-tune on larger datasets and models; no uncertainty estimates are reported for the evaluation scores.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; six matched CNN/Daily Mail scores across model sizes are retained. Other table results compare attention variants at a single size and do not bear on the tested version.

untested.parts: Predictability: no fitted curve or prediction, only two sizes, one dataset and one metric, no link to pretraining loss.
Not tested: no pretraining loss is measured.
Not tested: the attention variants change parameter counts and are applied at fine-tuning; no shape sweep is run.

missing.what: A footnote says T5-large reaches 46.3 R1 on Multi-news against 21.7 for T5-base MHA. T5-base is described as 'not trained on multi news', so the comparison is unclear and not like-for-like; it is probably not usable for V6.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling evidence is a two-model, single-dataset aside with no stated parameter counts, no seeds and no uncertainty. The supports verdict rests on direction only. The claimed widening of the gap rests on a 0.2 R1 difference.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law form and orders of magnitude.
Prediction of larger-run loss from power laws fitted on small runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their dependence on compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
No pretraining-loss versus downstream-performance relationship is tested, and only two model sizes are compared on one dataset; no predictive curve is fitted.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices; curve bending.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuned T5-small vs T5-base, CNN/Daily Mail Rouge-1, with MHA, GQA and WGQA attention
relationships.reason: In all three configurations the larger model scores higher, by 0.9 to 1.6 R1 (r1-r6). This shows direction only, not predictability.
relationships.display_finding: The larger model improves Rouge-1 by 0.9–1.6 points across MHA, GQA and WGQA, without establishing predictive scaling.
